quote: In this episode recorded in March 2022 we chatted with Rohit Gupta , founder and impact investor at Future Communities Capital (FCC) focused on mission-driven companies across all industries with a slight bend toward healthcare because of how the fund started and Rohit’s own background in the biotech space.

claim: The episode notes attribute Future Communities Capital's origin to an interest in healthtech, biotech, and opportunities for large-scale change.

quote: Unique differentiator - focused on mission-driven companies primarily but not exclusively in healthcare and committed to delivering value via high-value intros to accelerate sales (e.g. a novel healthtech looking to sell to health systems)
claim: The episode notes describe the firm's approach as backing mission-driven companies and helping them obtain valuable introductions that can accelerate sales.

quote: Key is to identify that the founder knows the industry they are selling to, have built trusted relationships with customers and are able and willing to roll up their sleeves and get their hands dirty.
claim: The episode notes attribute importance to founder industry knowledge, trusted customer relationships, and willingness to perform hands-on work.

quote: Prior to Series B / A, the metrics are often off anyways so it’s best to look at the model rather than the absolute numbers.

quote: Goal setting and plan-making is more important than the absolute numbers at the early stage.
claim: The episode notes report that early-stage goal setting and planning matter more than absolute numbers.

quote: Board formation is critical at the early stage for that reason.
claim: The episode notes characterize early-stage board formation as critical to maintaining alignment between founders and the board.

quote: We just did some early deals that,you know, our first for our first four deals were absolutely tremendous and that kind of startedthings for us.
